stem: The substantia nigra is located in which of the following regions of the brain:
fact: The substantia nigra is a nucleus in the midbrain.
finding: NCBI anatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: Which of the following clinical features is most suggestive of a lesion of the frontal lobe:
options: Conjugate eye deviation towards the side of the lesion
fact: A frontal-eye-field lesion causes conjugate eye deviation toward the side of the lesion.
mnemonic: Frontal eyes look toward the lesion.

stem: The blood supply to the parietal lobe is primarily supplied by which of the following arteries:
fact: The lateral parietal cortex is primarily supplied by the middle cerebral artery.
mnemonic: MCA covers much of the lateral convexity.
finding: NCBI MCA anatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: A 65 year old lady presents to ED complaining of visual loss. Examination demonstrates visual loss in the lower left quadrant in both visual fields. The lesion would most likely be in which of the following:
fact: Left lower homonymous quadrantanopia localizes to the right upper optic radiations, classically in the right parietal lobe.
finding: NCBI visual-pathway anatomy supports right parietal localization.

stem: The corpus callosum is composed of which type of fibres:
fact: The corpus callosum is a commissural fibre tract connecting the cerebral hemispheres.
finding: Standard neuroanatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: Which of the following is most likely to cause a homonymous hemianopia:
fact: A posterior cerebral artery stroke involving the occipital visual cortex can cause contralateral homonymous hemianopia, often with macular sparing.
finding: NCBI supports the displayed key and source explanation.

stem: The right and left cerebral hemispheres are partially separated by which of the following structures:
fact: The longitudinal fissure separates the cerebral hemispheres; the falx cerebri extends into it.
finding: Standard gross neuroanatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: What type of visual field defect are you most likely to see in a lesion of the optic tract:
fact: An optic-tract lesion causes contralateral homonymous hemianopia.
mnemonic: After the chiasm, visual loss is homonymous.

stem: Which of the following spinal tracts conveys nociceptive input from the contralateral side of the body:
fact: The lateral spinothalamic tract carries pain and temperature information; the source's contralateral-side wording is retained literally.
finding: NCBI supports the tract function; literal source wording is preserved.

stem: Which of the following best describes the function of the foramen of Monro:
options: Major site of production of CSF
Connects the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle
Drains CSF into the subarachnoid cisterns
Connects the third ventricle to the fourth ventricle
Connects the right and left lateral ventricles
fact: The interventricular foramen of Monro connects each lateral ventricle with the third ventricle.
mnemonic: Monro moves CSF from lateral to third.
finding: NCBI ventricular anatomy supports the displayed key.
